title: Sunrise Electricals plans ahead
body: Sunrise Electricals is a medium-sized maker of fans and coolers in Nagpur. Its managers hold a meeting every quarter to study changes outside the company: new government rules, changes in customer tastes, the plans of rival firms and new technologies. At one such meeting the marketing head reported that two large companies were about to enter the cooler market in central India. The managers did not wait for sales to fall. They decided to revise their pricing and distribution plan for the next three years and laid down new guidelines for dealing with dealers and offering after-sales service.

title: India in June 1991
body: In 1990-91 India's fiscal deficit reached about 6.6 per cent of GDP and interest payments were using up a large part of the central government's revenue. Inflation was running at 13-14 per cent. Foreign exchange reserves fell so low that they could pay for only a few weeks of imports, and non-resident Indians were withdrawing their deposits. India's credit rating was cut, and the country was close to defaulting on its international payments. To raise foreign currency, gold was leased and pledged abroad. In July 1991, the Government announced a new industrial policy along with other economic reforms.

title: Nova Phones after the reforms
body: Nova Phones was set up in the 1980s and for many years sold landline telephone sets with little competition. After the economic reforms of 1991, many Indian and foreign firms entered the market, and customers began to compare features, prices and service before buying. Nova's management found that its existing staff lacked the skills needed to handle the new methods of design, sales and service that the market now required. It therefore set up a training programme for all employees and started hiring people with new skills, so that its workforce could meet the challenges of the changed environment.
